knowledge:
- key_parameters: gess_method=Defines the search algorithm in qSig (e.g., "CMAP", "LINCS", "gCMAP", "Fisher", "Cor") ;; refdb=Path to the reference database HDF5 file (e.g., "lincs", "lincs2", "cmap", or a custom HDF5 file path) ;; query=The query signature in qSig, which can be a list of up/down gene sets or a quantitative matrix/vector ;; workers=Integer defining the number of CPU cores for parallel processing of database chunks ;; tau=Logical in gess_lincs indicating whether to compute standardized Tau scores ;; type=Annotation system to use in tsea_* or dsea_* (e.g., "GO", "Reactome") ;; ont=GO ontology type in tsea_* or dsea_* ("BP", "MF", "CC", or "ALL") ;; higher/lower=Thresholds in gess_gcmap or gess_fisher to define gene sets from quantitative profiles
- alternatives: signatureSearchData=Helper package providing pre-built CMAP2, LINCS, and LINCS2 databases via ExperimentHub ;; gCMAP package=Provides an alternative implementation of the CMAP algorithm, though signatureSearch implements its own gCMAP method ;; batchtools and BiocParallel=Used for scaling up GESS to computer clusters or multi-core local machines
- when_to_use: Appropriate when studying the effects of genetic, chemical, or environmental perturbations on biological systems, identifying novel modes of action (MOA) of bioactive compounds, or developing drug repurposing approaches using query gene expression signatures.
- pitfalls: Setting tau=TRUE in gess_lincs when using a small or toy database, as Tau values are only meaningful when the complete LINCS database is used ;; Standard enrichment methods eliminate target duplications, which is inappropriate for TSEA because many drugs share targets; users must use the specialized duplication-adjusted methods (dup_hyperG, mGSEA, mabs) provided by the package ;; Correlation-based methods require quantitative values of the same type for both query and database, making them highly technology-dependent compared to set-based methods.

workflows.name: gess_and_fea_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform a gene expression signature search (GESS) using a query signature against a reference database, followed by functional enrichment analysis (TSEA/DSEA) and drug-target network visualization.
input: query_mat (matrix of quantitative gene expression changes)
upset (character vector of up-regulated gene IDs)
downset (character vector of down-regulated gene IDs)
db_path (path to the reference HDF5 database file)
workflows.stages: 1. Initialize the query signature object using qSig ;; 2. Run GESS using a specific method (e.g., CMAP, LINCS, gCMAP, Fisher, or Cor) ;; 3. Extract search results using result ;; 4. Perform Target Set Enrichment Analysis (TSEA) using tsea_dup_hyperG, tsea_mGSEA, or tsea_mabs ;; 5. Perform Drug Set Enrichment Analysis (DSEA) using dsea_hyperG or dsea_GSEA ;; 6. Compare FEA results using comp_fea_res ;; 7. Visualize drug-target networks using dtnetplot
workflows.code:
qsig_cmap <- qSig(query = list(upset=upset, downset=downset), 
                  gess_method="CMAP", refdb=db_path)
cmap <- gess_cmap(qSig=qsig_cmap, chunk_size=5000, workers=1, addAnnotations = TRUE)
result(cmap)

qsig_lincs <- qSig(query=list(upset=upset, downset=downset), 
                   gess_method="LINCS", refdb=db_path)
lincs <- gess_lincs(qsig_lincs, sortby="NCS", tau=FALSE, workers=1, 
                    addAnnotations = TRUE, GeneType = "reference")
result(lincs)

qsig_gcmap <- qSig(query = query_mat, gess_method = "gCMAP", refdb = db_path)
gcmap <- gess_gcmap(qsig_gcmap, higher=1, lower=-1, workers=1, addAnnotations = TRUE)
result(gcmap)

qsig_fisher <- qSig(query = query_mat, gess_method = "Fisher", refdb = db_path)
fisher <- gess_fisher(qSig=qsig_fisher, higher=1, lower=-1, workers=1, addAnnotations = TRUE)
result(fisher)

qsig_sp <- qSig(query=query_mat, gess_method="Cor", refdb=db_path)
sp <- gess_cor(qSig=qsig_sp, method="spearman", workers=1, addAnnotations = TRUE)
result(sp)

drugs <- unique(result(lincs)$pert[1:10])
dup_hyperG_res <- tsea_dup_hyperG(drugs=drugs, universe="Default", 
                                  type="GO", ont="MF", pvalueCutoff=0.05, 
                                  pAdjustMethod="BH", qvalueCutoff=0.1, 
                                  minGSSize=10, maxGSSize=500)
result(dup_hyperG_res)

dup_rct_res <- tsea_dup_hyperG(drugs=drugs, type="Reactome",
                               pvalueCutoff=0.5, qvalueCutoff=0.5, readable=TRUE)
result(dup_rct_res)

mgsea_res <- tsea_mGSEA(drugs=drugs, type="GO", ont="MF", exponent=1, 
                        nPerm=1000, pvalueCutoff=1, minGSSize=5)
result(mgsea_res)

mabs_res <- tsea_mabs(drugs=drugs, type="GO", ont="MF", nPerm=1000, 
                      pvalueCutoff=0.05, minGSSize=5)
result(mabs_res)

hyperG_res <- dsea_hyperG(drugs=drugs, type="GO", ont="MF")
result(hyperG_res)

dl <- abs(result(lincs)$NCS); names(dl) <- result(lincs)$pert
dl <- dl[dl>0]
dl <- dl[!duplicated(names(dl))]
gsea_res <- dsea_GSEA(drugList=dl, type="GO", ont="MF", exponent=1, nPerm=1000,
                      pvalueCutoff=0.2, minGSSize=5)
result(gsea_res)

table_list = list("dup_hyperG" = result(dup_hyperG_res), 
                  "mGSEA" = result(mgsea_res), 
                  "mabs" = result(mabs_res), 
                  "hyperG" = result(hyperG_res), 
                  "GSEA" = result(gsea_res))
comp_fea_res(table_list, rank_stat="pvalue", Nshow=20)

dtnetplot(drugs = drugs(dup_hyperG_res), set = "GO:0032041", ont = "MF", 
          desc="NAD-dependent histone deacetylase activity (H3-K14 specific)")

workflows.name: batch_gess_processing
workflows.intent: Process multiple query signatures in parallel using multi-core CPUs or cluster environments.
input: batch_queries (list of query signatures containing upset and downset gene lists)
refdb (path to the reference HDF5 database file)
workflows.stages: 1. Define a list of query signatures ;; 2. Define a processing function that initializes qSig, runs gess_lincs, and writes results ;; 3. Execute parallel processing using bplapply (for multi-core) or batchMap/submitJobs (for cluster environments)
